solves.reason: The first sentence explicitly states 'Contingency implies selection and uncertainty' — certainty is wrong. Algorithms operate 'efficiently and reliably' — not creatively. We repair to 'restore their predictability' — not originality.
'algorithms are not contingent' is stated directly. 'neither unpredictable nor idiosyncratic' — unpredictable is correct. 'We repair them precisely' — repair, not replace.
'they do not choose between possibilities' — possibilities, not limitations. 'neither unpredictable nor idiosyncratic' — idiosyncratic fits. 'We do not care about the moods' — moods, not functions.
The passage says algorithms operate 'efficiently and reliably'. erratically means irregularly — the direct opposite of reliably. The other three words are contextually appropriate.
The passage says 'we think that it is broken'. innovative means new/creative — the opposite of broken. The other words fit their contexts.
The passage says algorithms 'operate so efficiently'. sluggishly means slowly/lazily — the opposite. instructions, indicate, and perspectives all fit.

'algorithms are not ____ — which is why they can operate so efficiently and reliably.' The causal link (which is why) connects to not being contingent. creative/original/reliable don't create this causal logic.

'Different watches should all indicate the same time to all users, if they work ____.' properly means correctly/as intended. efficiently and precisely are close but don't capture 'functioning correctly'.

'We repair them ____ to restore their predictability.' precisely means exactly/accurately, fitting the deliberate act of restoring predictability. reliably and creatively don't fit the repair context.
contingent = conditional. The passage defines contingency through selection and uncertainty — things that depend on circumstances. permanent/systematic/trivial are unrelated.
idiosyncratic = peculiar (unique/distinctive to an individual). predictable, conventional, universal are all antonyms or unrelated concepts.
restore = bring back (return to previous state). eliminate means remove, increase means grow, establish means create new — none mean returning to a prior state.
uncertainty ↔ assurance. ambiguity and doubt are near-synonyms of uncertainty. complexity is about difficulty, not certainty.
reliably ↔ erratically. steadily/consistently/securely all share the positive direction of reliability. Only erratically means unpredictably/irregularly.
(A) 'instructions that program their behavior' = to code/program digitally. (B) 'program a series of workshops, scheduling them' = to plan/schedule. Different senses.
'a possible future event or condition that cannot be predicted with certainty' = contingency. An algorithm is a procedure; instruction is a directive; perspective is a viewpoint.
Parallel with 'reliably' (adverb). 'so ____ and reliably' — both must be adverbs modifying 'operate'. efficient (adj) → efficiently (adv).
'their ____' needs a noun. The context is restoring the trait of being predictable. predict → predictability (the quality of being predictable), not prediction (the act of predicting).
'designed to ____ that program their behavior' — follow the instructions. Algorithms don't choose between possibilities (the passage explicitly says they don't choose).

'we expect algorithms to be ____, even when they deliver information.' The passage explicitly says 'neither unpredictable nor idiosyncratic'. creative/original contradicts the thesis; efficient/reliable is a different clause.
